bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Why timing is non-negotiable for New Guinea Singing Dogs: each booster lands after the previous dose’s immunology window, usually every 2–4 weeks, until the New Guinea Singing Dog series closes at about 16 weeks.
Size class small does not invent new viruses for the New Guinea Singing Dog, but it does change crate fit, blood-draw ease, and how early you lock travel relative to the final DA2PP / DHPP booster.
Flag parasite risk if wild-type husbandry at New Guinea Singing Dog vaccine checkups so the puppy’s chart accumulates breed-relevant context, not just sticker dates.
When the New Guinea Singing Dog series is complete, switch reminders to adult booster cadence instead of deleting the vaccine thread entirely.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: If your New Guinea Singing Dog misses the dose scheduled near week 12, call the clinic the same day with product names — do not restart the New Guinea Singing Dog series from memory.
The danger for a delayed New Guinea Singing Dog is the gap, not the embarrassment, because parvovirus pressure stays real for an under-vaccinated puppy even in clean-looking neighborhoods.
While waiting for the make-up DA2PP / DHPP visit, skip high-traffic dog parks / unknown-cat intros and keep the New Guinea Singing Dog away from unvaccinated animals.
After catch-up, rewrite reminders for the next New Guinea Singing Dog due date (7, 3, and 1 day prior) so the same miss does not recur.

faqs.question: When does the New Guinea Singing Dog core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my New Guinea Singing Dog misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.
